bibliographic.title: A review for navigating the trade-offs: evaluating open-source and proprietary large language models for clinical and biomedical information extraction
bibliographic.authors: Sugihara, Y.; Milosavljevic, A.; Jankovskaja, S.; Falk, M.
bibliographic.citation_apa: Sugihara, Y., Milosavljevic, A., Jankovskaja, S., & Falk, M. (2026). A review for navigating the trade-offs: evaluating open-source and proprietary large language models for clinical and biomedical information extraction. Frontiers in Digital Health, 8, 1778786. https://doi.org/10.3389/fdgth.2026.1778786

methodology.method_family: narrative or integrative literature review with multi-axis evaluation framework
methodology.study_design: review comparing open-source and proprietary LLMs across five axes for clinical and biomedical information extraction
methodology.technology_context: large language models for clinical and biomedical information extraction workflows including named entity recognition, relation extraction, and terminology normalization; open-source versus proprietary models; mentions RAG, PHI, HIPAA, and GDPR

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article is a peer-reviewed review of LLMs for clinical and biomedical information extraction that explicitly evaluates transparency, auditability, patient-centric governance, accountability, compliance, privacy, and bias in regulated healthcare. It does not address conversational AI, chatbots, agents, or conversational governance workflows, so it is relevant as supporting rather than central evidence for a review focused on conversational governance.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Only front matter and introductory pages were provided; full review methodology, search strategy, inclusion criteria, and synthesis methods are not visible. Conversational relevance is absent and must be confirmed at full-text level.

appraisal.notes: Appraisal is based on limited excerpt (pages 1-2). The review states a clear comparative objective and a five-axis framework, but search strategy, study selection, and synthesis procedures are not shown in the provided text.

cerqual.explanation: The review coherently frames OSS versus proprietary LLM trade-offs for clinical IE and governance dimensions, but adequacy of the underlying literature synthesis cannot be judged from the excerpt provided.

coding.theme: Governance-oriented trade-offs between open-source and proprietary LLMs in clinical information extraction
coding.subtheme: Transparency, auditability, and patient-centric governance in regulated healthcare AI
rq_alignment: risk and compliance in healthcare AI

synthesis.main_claim: Open-source and proprietary LLMs present distinct trade-offs for clinical and biomedical information extraction, with proprietary models stronger on schema compliance and complex reasoning while open-source models offer greater auditability, local control, cost-effectiveness, and customization for privacy-sensitive healthcare tasks.
synthesis.contribution: Provides a five-axis review framework—performance, reproducibility, cost, transparency and auditability, and patient-centric governance—for comparing OSS and proprietary LLMs in clinical IE workflows.
synthesis.limitations: Provided text does not describe the full review protocol, search methods, or number of included studies; scope is narrowed to information extraction rather than broader clinical NLP or conversational systems.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as supporting evidence on LLM governance trade-offs, transparency, auditability, accountability, and compliance in regulated healthcare, not as primary evidence on conversational governance, chatbots, or agentic oversight.
